purpose: Prednisolone is used to reduce inflammation and calm down your immune system when it is overreacting. It helps treat a wide range of conditions including asthma, allergies, arthritis, skin problems, and certain autoimmune diseases. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other conditions where swelling or an overactive immune response is causing problems.
how_it_works: Prednisolone works by mimicking a natural hormone your body already makes called cortisol. It tells your immune system to calm down and reduces the chemicals in your body that cause swelling, redness, and irritation. Think of it as a powerful anti-inflammatory switch that helps your body stop overreacting.
common_side_effects: Increased appetite and weight gain, trouble sleeping, mood changes or feeling more emotional, upset stomach, increased blood sugar levels, acne, and feeling more thirsty or needing to urinate more often. Long-term use can also weaken bones and lower your resistance to infections.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, especially if you have been taking it for more than a few weeks, as this can make you very unwell. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, or any infections. Avoid contact with people who have chickenpox or measles while on this medication. Let all your healthcare providers know you are taking a steroid.
typical_dosing: The dose varies widely depending on what condition is being treated. Adults commonly take anywhere from 5 mg to 60 mg once a day, usually in the morning with food to reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will set the right dose for you and may gradually lower it over time. Always follow your prescription instructions carefully.
